fields.AN_Notes: Own benchmark MGBR on 23 LLMs. Techniques tested: Zero-shot+CoT ('Let's think step by step.'), Few-shot with pro-stereotypical demonstrations (ICL), Debiasing Prompt as General_Guidance with the strategy 'Please ensure that your answer is unbiased and does not rely on stereotypes.' Mitigation evaluated: CoT reduces bias scores, the debiasing instruction is reported as inadequate (own experiment, Tables 1 and 4). Harm: LLMs classify gender-neutral occupations as feminine or masculine (occupational stereotypes). Bias is determined technically through the accuracy-difference bias score. Gender treated as binary word categories, the limitation states binary gender only. No theory frames gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Research agenda for a feminist metaethics of AI in four lines: theory vs action, real-life effects of AI ethics, agents of AI ethics, topics and methods. Gender and its interaction with class, race, disability and sexuality are part of the work's own proposed analysis of AI impact; no empirical bias analysis. Harm types: the work argues about effects of AI ethics discourse (ethics-washing, ethics-shopping, ethics as branding, ethics-bashing), which the Gallegos taxonomy does not cover, and names AI harm cases (image classification, gaydar, gendered automation effects) only as illustrative case studies, so None. Mitigation proposed at organisational level: diversity and representativeness of AI ethics boards, inclusion of those hitherto ignored in decision-making. Gender is not defined; the intersectional feminist frame makes the understanding recognisable. Bias in the sense of structural domination and oppression is framed, not defined.

fields.AN_Notes: German conference handout on power and digitalisation in social work with case vignettes and reflection questions. Other_Axis: place of residence (Stadtteil), used as worked example of proxy discrimination. Axes coded from the work's own case examples (child-welfare algorithm and migration background, social-assistance AI and Black and migrant applicants, debt scoring and low-income districts, job-centre scoring by age, school education and district); Frauen, disability and language appear only in enumerations of affected groups and are not coded. Harm: Direct_Discrimination where the score uses origin itself (scoring features 'Einkommen, Alter, Herkunft'), Indirect_Discrimination via district as proxy, Exclusionary_Norms via digital-only access to benefits. Mitigation proposed at organisational and political level: participation of professionals and clients, human control, transparency and right to object, reflection methods ('Macht-Check', Ethik-Cafés), regulation and ban of discriminatory systems. AI tasks: risk assessment and scoring (case assessment), AI chat tool helping clients with applications (client communication), ChatGPT-connected avatar Konrad for workshops and social-media teaching. Gender is no object of the work. Bias is described as prejudice carried from old data into algorithms without a definition.

fields.AN_Notes: DR.GAP system prompt: bias-revealing demonstrations (ICL), stepwise syllogistic CoT reasoning (Thought_Generation), reasoning verification and iterative refinement by a reference model (Self_Criticism), persona line 'You are a fair and impartial assistant who avoids gender bias as much as possible in your answers.' (Role_Persona). Evaluated on coreference and QA benchmarks and VisoGender against CFD and DPO baselines (own experiment, Tables 2 and 3); the DPO baseline is a comparator, not the work's intervention, so only Prompt_Practice is coded. Harms from own results: stereotypical gender-occupation associations, accuracy gap between masculine and feminine pronouns (Delta G), VLMs defaulting to male pronouns. Bias determined through the benchmark metrics. Gender binary by stated scope.

fields.AN_Notes: Qualitative interviews with 63 employees of an anonymised tech multinational, analysed with feminist methods (Ahmed's storytelling approach, Haraway's situated knowledges). Gender axis from the authors' own worked example against interviewee #35 (Wikipedia training data underrepresent women); race and other minoritised groups appear only in enumerations. Harm Erasure: data about women less likely represented. Mitigation proposed at organisational level: bring DEI initiatives and AI ethics goals together, prioritise maintenance and monitoring of AI and legacy systems, involve tech workers. Gender (with race) explicitly determined as a set of relations rather than personal attributes. Bias reframed explicitly as 'AI partiality'.
